paper_title: Systems Scale Interactive Exploration Reveals Quantitative and Qualitative Differences in Response to Influenza and Pneumococcal Vaccines
overall_main_claims: Influenza and pneumococcal vaccines induce distinct blood transcriptional responses with different magnitudes and kinetics.
Influenza vaccination elicits an early interferon-dominated innate transcriptional signature detectable within hours.
Pneumococcal vaccination elicits a stronger inflammation-associated innate signature and a more prominent day 7 plasmablast signature.
Day 1 and day 7 blood transcriptional/module signatures correlate with later antibody responses.

assays.sample_type: whole blood collected in Tempus blood RNA tubes; capillary blood collected by finger stick for early time-course profiling; isolated neutrophils, monocytes, CD4+ T cells, and CD8+ T cells for subset profiling
readout: differentially expressed transcripts over time after vaccination
downstream_analysis: background subtraction, log2 transformation, quantile normalization
differential expression versus prevaccination baseline using linear mixed models with FDR control
fold-change filtering
heatmap visualization of 239 responsive transcripts
circular plot overlap analysis of differentially expressed gene lists across groups and time points
modular repertoire analysis using preexisting transcriptional modules
counting proportion of significant transcripts per module and defining responsive modules
module-level averaging of baseline-normalized expression
comparison of in vivo vaccine signatures with in vitro stimulation signatures by overlap/circular plots
Pearson correlation of module averages across validation cohorts
correlation of day 1/day 7 module signatures with serology results
pathway/functional interpretation of responsive modules

readout: frequencies and absolute numbers of leukocyte/B cell subsets
identification of plasmablasts/plasma cells as CD19+/lo CD20−CD27+CD38hi plasmablasts and plasma cells
absolute numbers of CD19+ B cells and plasmablasts over time
downstream_analysis: log2 transformation of continuous flow variables
linear mixed model testing across time points
kinetic plotting of absolute cell numbers
comparison of plasmablast expansion between influenza and pneumococcal vaccine groups

downstream_analysis: comparison of pre- and postvaccination antibody levels

assays.assay_name: In Vitro Stimulation with Innate Immune Ligands
assays.sample_type: fresh whole blood from healthy subjects incubated with innate immune stimuli or left unstimulated
readout: stimulus-induced blood transcriptional responses after 6 hr incubation
downstream_analysis: microarray-based profiling of stimulated samples
quantile normalization and filtering by detection p value

construction of in vitro gene lists for each stimulus
overlap analysis between in vitro stimulation signatures and in vivo vaccine signatures using circular plots

assays.sample_type: freshly ficolled PBMC and whole blood-derived leukocytes
readout: purified neutrophils, monocytes (CD14+), CD4+ T cells, and CD8+ T cells
downstream_analysis: used as input material for subset-specific microarray profiling to assign cellular contributors to the interferon signature

notes_for_later_claim_extraction: Do not create separate assay entries for module analysis, pathway analysis, circular plots, heatmaps, or correlation analysis; these are downstream analyses of microarray or serology outputs.
The in vitro stimulation experiment is best treated as a reference/annotation assay because it was used to interpret in vivo vaccine transcriptional signatures rather than as the main endpoint.

Subset-specific transcript profiling of neutrophils/monocytes/CD4+/CD8+ cells appears to use the same microarray platform as the whole-blood profiling; kept under the same Microarray Assay entry rather than split into a separate assay instance.
Flow cytometry is claim-supporting mainly for validating the plasmablast signature inferred from transcriptomics.
Serology comprises two distinct performed assay families in this paper: influenza HAI/virus-neutralization and pneumococcal commercial immunoassays.
CBC is mentioned in Methods as part of sample analysis but no explicit Results claim from CBC was visible in the provided pages.
